title: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS & FID
interviewAnswer: PSNR measures pixel-level fidelity, SSIM compares structural similarity, LPIPS uses deep features for perceptual similarity, and FID compares distributions of generated and real features. No single metric captures physical correctness.
why: Image reconstruction/generation interviews often probe whether you know that pixel similarity, perceptual quality and distributional realism are different objectives.
intuition: PSNR asks how close pixels are, SSIM compares local structural patterns, LPIPS compares deep perceptual features, and FID compares feature distributions across sets of images.
deepDive: PSNR is a logarithmic transform of MSE and rewards pixel fidelity. SSIM uses luminance/contrast/structure comparisons. LPIPS measures distance in pretrained deep feature spaces and often aligns better with perception. FID fits Gaussians to Inception features of real/generated image sets and compares their means/covariances; it is distribution-level and sensitive to sample size/domain mismatch. None guarantees physical correctness for scientific images.
workedExample: A slightly shifted reconstruction can have poor PSNR despite looking perceptually similar; a generative model can have good FID while failing to reproduce the exact input. Choose metrics to match the task.
code:
# PSNR from MSE for images normalized to [0,1]
import math
psnr = 10*math.log10(1.0/mse)
commonMistakes: Using FID for one image pair.
Interpreting high PSNR as proof of physical validity.
Comparing FID values computed with different feature pipelines/sample counts as if directly equivalent.
followUps: Why can diffusion have low PSNR but useful samples?
What metric would you use for scientific microstructures?
production: Define task-specific acceptance metrics alongside generic image metrics. For scientific/engineering vision, validate domain properties and downstream simulations, not aesthetics alone.
